title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (FP8 + FP4 experts) on 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB: TP8+EP8, short/long request matrix C1-C32, and why TP4 does not fit

hardware.interconnect: PCIe only, no NVLink; GPU0-3 NODE within NUMA0, GPU4-7 NODE within NUMA1, cross-group SYS
hardware.topology_summary: nvidia-smi topo -m: 4+4 split across two CPU sockets
hardware.cpu_numa: 2 x Xeon Platinum 8488C, 192 threads; GPU0-3 -> NUMA0, GPU4-7 -> NUMA1; 1.5 TB RAM

software.clocks: not locked; default application clocks (idle 180 MHz, max 3090 MHz); 300 W power cap

model.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (538B-class MoE, 40 layers, 384 routed experts / 6 active, MLA attention with Engram tables)
model.quantization: FP8 block 32x32 weights (ue8m0 scales) + FP4 packed experts (expert_dtype=fp4); 476 GiB on disk

workload.input_tokens: 256 (short) / 8192 (long) requested; measured prompts average ~120 and ~4,744 tokens. The random-ids dataset is re-tokenized through the chat template, so the effective prompt is 47-58% of the nominal length. Verified not to be a prefix-cache artefact: a companion run with --disable-radix-cache shows the same per-request lengths
workload.output_tokens: 128 (short) / 256 (long) requested; the model stops at EOS after ~62 (short) and ~119 (long) tokens, so the reported output totals are lower than the cap
workload.sampling: temperature 0, top_p 1.0, seed 42, one warm-up request per level
workload.server_notes: TP8 + EP8, --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4, dsv4/flashmla attention, --chunked-prefill-size 2048, --max-running-requests 32, --mem-fraction-static 0.85, --context-length 32768, CUDA graph decode bs<=32. Startup reports max_total_num_tokens=12443136 and 9.10 GiB available for KV, i.e. ~785 B/token on this build

commands.server: sglang serve --model-path /models2/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-cfg0 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --ep-size 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --max-running-requests 32 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16 --context-length 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8200  (env: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=2097152, SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1, SGLANG_DSV41_TORCH_PREFILL_INDEXER=1, SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1) Container mounts: -v /path/to/models:/models2:ro -v /path/to/patches/full_topk.py:/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/v41_indexer/full_topk.py:ro (read-only patch baked into the launch; without it the dsv4 indexer path differs)
commands.client: python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8200 --model <local path> --tokenizer <local path> --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len {256|8192} --random-output-len {128|256} --num-prompts {16 | 2*concurrency} --max-concurrency {1,4,8,16,32} --seed 42 --disable-tqdm

variance.note: Three independent server launches (container restart between runs, weights reloaded each time). Long-request levels reproduce within 0.1-3.2%; short-request levels at c4-c16 spread 14-128%, worst at c8. Per-config arrays below.

methodology: Three independent launches of the same server command; each level is one bench_serving invocation with one warm-up request, random-ids prompts (fixed seed), fixed input/output lengths, temperature 0. Metrics are wall-clock from the client; TTFT/TPOT come from the streaming responses. Throughput in the results table is the mean of the three launches; p99 TTFT is the worst observed.
transferable: On 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB (SM120, PCIe, dual NUMA), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 runs at TP8+EP8 with 476 GiB of weights and a 12.4M-token KV pool on the dev-minimax image

Long-request (8192/256) aggregate output peaks at c8 (252.9 tok/s mean) and then falls to 189.2 at c16 and 216.6 at c32 - prefill and decode contend for the same SMs, which is the case PD separation targets
Long-request levels are the reproducible part of this dataset: 0.1-3.2% spread across three launches
Single-stream decode is ~34 tok/s (TPOT 24.8 ms) for both shapes, i.e. concurrency buys aggregate throughput, not per-stream speed
not_transferable: Short-request levels are NOT reproducible on this build: c4-c16 spread 14-128% across launches (c8 measured 71.4, 71.8 and 162.6 tok/s in three runs), so do not quote the short-request curve as a configuration result

The effective prompt is 47-58% of the nominal length (random-ids is re-tokenized through the chat template), so input throughput is not 'an 8192-token prompt'. The companion cache-off dataset shows how much prefix caching contributes to the difference
Output length is model-determined (EOS at ~62 / ~119 tokens), not the 128/256 cap; token throughput is not comparable to fixed-length runs
TP4 is impossible for this checkpoint on 4 x 72 GB: 476 GiB / 4 = 119 GiB per card against 71.12 GiB usable, and the load OOMs at 70.74 GiB. See docs/09-failures.md F-16
Absolute numbers depend on the exact image digest, driver/CUDA, the three SM120 patches, and --max-running-requests 32 (the production compose uses 8)
